papers.title: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families
papers.abstract: LLM-guided program evolution can produce mathematical constructions, but validity, generality, and reproducibility require distinct evidence. We develop a researcher-in-the-loop discovery pipeline that combines program evolution, exact evaluation, mathematical generalization, certified nonexistence checks, and formal proof checking. We apply it to entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes (EAQECCs). Starting from tasks that did not specify a family formula, evolved programs produced finite qubit constructions whose structure researchers generalized to the family $[[n,1,n-1;n-q-1]]_q$ for prime powers $q\ge3$ at $n\ge2q+1$ and for $q=2$ at odd $n\ge5$. Lean checks the algebraic certificate underlying this family. Together with entanglement lifting, the family closes 54 gaps in archived EAQECC tables. The released evidence includes 115 verified code records, ten nonexistence results with checked DRAT proofs, family implementations, and preserved search programs for exact checks and seeded replay. In a controlled cohort of eight paired generation blocks, validation-selected iterative programs achieve success in 46.1% and 31.6% of held-out executions at unseen lengths $n=13,15$, compared with 19.5% and 3.1% for independently generated programs. In this setting, program evolution and researcher analysis turn finite computational discoveries into a proved family with independently checkable evidence.

papers.title: Optimal Multi-bit Generative Watermarking Schemes Under Worst-Case False-Alarm Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper considers the problem of multi-bit generative watermarking for large language models under a worst-case false-alarm constraint. Prior work established a lower bound on the achievable miss-detection probability in the finite-token regime and proposed a scheme claimed to achieve this bound. We show, however, that the proposed scheme is in fact suboptimal. We then develop two new encoding-decoding constructions that attain the previously established lower bound, thereby completely characterizing the optimal multi-bit watermarking performance. Our approach formulates the watermark design problem as a linear program and derives the structural conditions under which optimality can be achieved. In addition, we identify the failure mechanism of the previous construction and compare the tradeoffs between the two proposed schemes.

papers.title: Towards Diverse and Comprehensive Benchmarks for Mutual Information Estimation
papers.abstract: Mutual information estimation is a central problem in machine learning and statistics; however, existing benchmarks typically evaluate estimators on simplified, low-dimensional distributions, leaving their performance on complex, realistic data largely unexplored. We address this gap with a comprehensive benchmarking framework grounded in a unified copula-theoretic perspective that subsumes existing benchmarks as special cases. Within this framework, we propose two complementary families of tests: a copula-first family that systematically varies ground-truth mutual information, dimensionality, and marginal complexity using synthetic and flow-based transformations; and a marginals-first family that couples real-world image data with controlled dependency structures, extending the classic same-class-pairing paradigm. We use this suite to extensively evaluate three classes of estimators: non-parametric, variational, and generative. Contrary to prevailing assumptions, our results indicate that there is no universal winner: each category can systematically outperform all other estimators under specific setups. By analyzing these cases, we identify fundamental estimation barriers and propose new tests that more effectively stress these specific limitations. We share the open source code at https://github.com/VanessB/mutinfo.

papers.title: The Pareto Secretary Problem
papers.abstract: The Pareto secretary problem asks for online selection of a Pareto-maximal observation from an i.i.d. sample: no other observation is at least as good in every coordinate and strictly better in one. For every fixed dimension $d\ge2$ and independent continuous coordinates, the optimal failure probability is of order $1/[(\log n)^{d-1}\log\log n]$, both with full information and with coordinate ranks alone. A deterministic rank rule attains the optimal leading term uniformly over the marginals. For every fixed positive definite Gaussian covariance, the same failure order holds, with a leading constant depending on the correlation matrix, and a rank-based rule attains the optimal leading failure probability without knowing the Gaussian parameters. In both models, we determine the optimal fixed cutoff and its leading failure constant; its failure probability exceeds the unrestricted optimum by a factor $\Theta_d((\log\log n)^2)$. Under arbitrary dependence, a fixed joint density with uniform marginals can instead have optimal full-information success tending to approximately $0.58$. The proof uses the scarcity of observations with very small domination probability to bound every stopping rule. A matching rule selects a currently maximal point when this probability is below a threshold that increases as time runs out. Coordinate ranks from an initial sample provide sufficiently accurate estimates to preserve the optimal leading failure probability. For singular Gaussian distributions with known correlations, we characterize the optimal failure asymptotics attainable using ranks. Singular dependence can make every observation acceptable or recover the difficulty of selecting a single best point.

papers.title: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources
papers.abstract: Estimating biased finite-memory sources from a single trajectory is a fundamental problem with practical impact, for example in estimating entropy for cryptography. We study order-$d$ binary sources whose conditional probabilities have bias at most $\epsilon$, and establish *sharp* sample complexity bounds: relative accuracy $\gamma$ with confidence $1-\delta$ needs $\gamma^{-2}\,(\tfrac12-\epsilon)^{-d}\,(\log d+\log\tfrac1\delta)$ samples up to constants depending on $\epsilon$, with matching upper and lower bounds and no dependence on mixing time or spectral gap. The proof rests on a sharp bound on expected hitting times of the sliding-window (de Bruijn) chain, which stay of order $1/\pi(w)$ uniformly in $d$ exactly when $\epsilon<\tfrac3{10}$, and on majorization of the window masses by those of independent biased coins. Applied to published entropy-source validations, the bounds show that their trace lengths may be underpowered: $10^6$ bits cannot resolve all transitions of an $8$-bit model to better than about $4.5\%$ relative error.

papers.title: Privacy-Constrained Function Computation in Distributed Databases
papers.abstract: Consider distributed databases that contain both sensitive (private) and non-sensitive (public) attributes. A user seeks to compute a function of public attributes and side information by interacting with the databases and downloading their responses. In this paper, we study the trade-offs among download cost, information leakage about the private attributes, and distortion between the computed function and its reconstruction, referred to as the capacity region. Our main contributions are as follows. For a single database, we provide a complete characterization of the capacity region for general discrete sources and characterize the capacity region of two different setups for Gaussian sources when the computed function is defined as the sum of the public attribute and side information. For distributed databases, we establish inner and outer bounds on the capacity region of discrete sources and we characterize the capacity region when the databases and the side information are mutually independent. As a special instance, we study lossless function computation, and results analogous to the lossy case are obtained.

papers.title: On the Communication-Sensing Tradeoff in DMT-Optimal Space-time-Coded ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) has been extensively studied from the perspective of communication-sensing performance tradeoffs. In MIMO communication systems, the diversity-multiplexing tradeoff (DMT) fundamentally characterizes the tradeoff between communication reliability and multiplexing gain, and DMT-optimal space-time codes achieve this optimal tradeoff without instantaneous channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT), making them particularly attractive for ISAC scenarios where accurate CSIT is difficult to acquire or maintain. In this work, we propose an analytical framework for characterizing the sensing behavior and communication-sensing gain tradeoff of DMT-optimal space-time codes in ISAC systems. Under a single-target detection model, we propose the sensing diversity order as the high-SNR sensing reliability metric. We further show that a class of DMT-optimal space-time codes, exemplified by Perfect codes, eliminates sensing blind spots for all nonzero codewords, thereby achieving joint DMT-sensing-diversity (DMTS) optimality. Furthermore, using the Perfect code as a representative DMT-optimal construction, we show that its isotropic average transmit covariance limits the achievable sensing gain when the target angular region is narrow. We therefore develop a full-rank spatial precoding framework and a low-complexity surrogate precoder that preserve joint DMTS optimality while shaping the transmit beampattern. Simulation results show that, for a target angular region of $\theta\in[-\pi/10,\pi/10]$, the proposed design achieves approximately 3 dB sensing-gain improvement over the unprecoded Perfect code.

papers.title: POST-MIMO: Partition-Oriented Semantic Transmission for MIMO Point Cloud Delivery
papers.abstract: Point clouds have become a fundamental data format for emerging three dimensional (3D) applications, while their wireless delivery remains challenging due to the large data volume and irregular geometric structure. Existing semantic point cloud transmission methods are mainly developed for single-input single-output systems, making them difficult to apply directly to multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To address this issue, we propose a partition-oriented semantic transmission framework for MIMO (POST-MIMO) point cloud delivery. POST-MIMO partitions the input point cloud into spatially coherent blocks and aligns them with parallel MIMO streams. Based on this block-aligned representation, the transmitter employs a hierarchical encoder to capture both intra-block local geometry and inter-block global dependency, while the auxiliary side information is transmitted jointly to assist reconstruction. At the receiver, a progressive decoder reconstructs the block geometry in a progressive manner and restores the final point cloud with block-aware adjustment. Experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and lower computational resource consumption than representative reference schemes under the considered MIMO setting.

papers.title: Scaled-Gradient Hard Thresholding Algorithms for Sparse Signal Recovery
papers.abstract: Thresholding methods provide a simple iterative framework for sparse signal recovery by combining a search direction with a thresholding operation. Gradient-based search directions are computationally efficient because they require only first-order information for the error metric. We incorporate componentwise gradient scaling into this framework by preserving large-magnitude components and attenuating the remaining components of the gradient of error metric. Combining this strategy with hard thresholding yields scaled-gradient hard thresholding (SGHT) and its pursuit variant SGHTP. Under suitable restricted isometry conditions, we establish recovery error bounds for both methods that account for measurement noise and deviations from exact sparsity. Numerical experiments indicate that SGHTP achieves recovery performance comparable to established pursuit methods on the tested ECG signals.

papers.title: Beamfocusing Beyond the Near Field: Frequency Diverse Arrays for OFDM-ISAC Systems
papers.abstract: Traditional phased arrays (PAs) achieve near-field (NF) beamfocusing through spherical wavefront curvature, but lose this range selectivity in the far field (FF). Frequency diverse arrays (FDAs) instead introduce frequency offsets across antenna elements. These offsets synthesize a range-dependent beam whose beamdepth is governed by the aggregate frequency-offset span rather than the physical aperture, thereby extending finite beamdepth into the FF. Although FDAs have been extensively studied for radar, their broader potential for wireless communications remains largely unexplored. Accordingly, this article examines how this capability can support wireless communications and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). We compare PA and FDA focusing mechanisms, explain FDA coupling and periodicities, and assess coexistence with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM). Integer-multiple offsets preserve alignment with the OFDM subcarrier grid and avoid offset-induced intercarrier interference under ideal synchronization, but require suitable symbol mapping and receiver processing. We also distinguish FDA beamdepth from waveform-based radar range resolution and discuss their complementary roles in sensing. For the configurations studied, FDAs offer no additional single-user spatial degrees of freedom. Interestingly, their principal benefit is multiuser separation through location division multiple access (LDMA). Numerical case studies under an idealized FDA channel model show that FDA-LDMA achieves higher sum-rates than PA-based schemes for users with small angular separation in the FF, even after accounting for the bandwidth reserved for frequency offsets.

papers.title: LEO Constellation Analysis for Satellite IoT: An Analysis of Coverage Gaps and Retransmissions
papers.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations are a promising way to connect Internet of Things (IoT) devices beyond terrestrial coverage, yet the intermittent visibility of their satellites imposes hard constraints on system and protocol design. Coverage probability and other snapshot statistics, which are often computed without accounting for the terminal's latitude, are insufficient for this purpose. Designers also need the temporal structure of coverage: the rate of coverage gaps, their duration distribution and mean, and quantities such as the probability that a retransmission succeeds after an initial transmission has failed. We develop an ergodic framework for Walker Star constellations in which these quantities reduce to spatial integrals over a two-dimensional torus that can be evaluated efficiently. We validate the framework against a seven-day Simplified General Perturbations 4 (SGP4) simulation of the Iridium NEXT constellation and find close agreement for the coverage probability, the revisit-time distribution, and the retransmission success probability. A comparison of Walker Star configurations further shows that constellations with similar satellite counts can yield substantially different packet-delivery probabilities with at most one retransmission, depending on the number of orbital planes. The results show that the ergodic model accurately gives the long-run values that finite time-domain simulations can only approximate, providing researchers with a tractable basis for the analytical modelling of IoT connectivity over non-terrestrial networks (NTN).

papers.title: Secure Deterministic Identification with Feedback and Sensing over State-Dependent Wiretap Channels
papers.abstract: Identification differs from classical transmission in that the receiver determines whether a particular identity was sent rather than recovering a message. We study secure deterministic identification over state-dependent discrete memoryless wiretap channels with private noiseless feedback and a sensing distortion constraint. The encoder has no local randomness and uses only the identity and past feedback. A symbol-wise input restriction guarantees the sensing constraint. We show that the secure deterministic identification capacity equals its non-secure feedback counterpart when the admissible main channel has positive ordinary transmission capacity and H(Y|Z,X=x)>0 for some fixed admissible input x. This equality does not require positive classical wiretap secrecy capacity. For achievability, noiseless feedback generates common randomness for identification and enables secret-key extraction by privacy amplification. The extracted key one-time-pad encrypts a short identification tag, whose reliable transmission requires only a sublinear number of additional channel uses. We also present an alternative construction in which feedback-generated randomness replaces the local randomization of a stochastic wiretap encoder. We further prove that secure identification capacity vanishes whenever non-secure identification capacity is zero. We also identify a class of channels with input-independent wiretapper observations that achieves full non-secure identification capacity even when the private conditional feedback entropy is zero, illustrated by a binary state-dependent wiretap channel. Thus, feedback can support both identification and secrecy without local encoder randomization while satisfying sensing constraints.

papers.title: Shaping and Finite-Blocklength Analysis of Quaternionic Alamouti-Type Codes
papers.abstract: We study finite $2\times2$ Alamouti-type space--time codes associated with classical maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over $\mathbb Q$. For the family indexed by primes $q\equiv3\pmod4$, we prove that the Eisenstein case $q=3$ uniquely minimises the finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum lattice distance and alphabet size. This ordering holds for every integer $p\geq2$, including when the representatives and their common translation are jointly optimised, with an explicit positive gap for every $q>3$. For uniform finite inputs, we derive a controlled high-SNR expansion of the information variance and determine its limiting ratio to the mutual information deficit. The mutual information expansion specialises arbitrary input fading results and gives an explicit remainder. Standard random-coding and second-order achievability tools relate these quantities to reliability over independently faded Alamouti blocks. All alphabets preserve symbol-wise maximum-likelihood detection at the Alamouti level. Numerical energy, mutual information, and error-rate comparisons support the analysis. Centred comparisons with classical Alamouti, Golden, and Silver codes illustrate the trade-off between reliability, symbol rate, and decoding effort.

papers.title: Feasibility of Common-Stream-Only Sensing in ZF-RSMA with Imperfect CSIT
papers.abstract: Reusing the Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) common stream for sensing eliminates dedicated probing signals in Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC), but creates a feasibility bottleneck: the common-power fraction must simultaneously support common decoding, private decoding, and target detection. This paper investigates this tradeoff in downlink zero-forcing RSMA with imperfect channel state information at the transmitter (CSIT) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC). With the common beam fixed over a sensing dwell through sensing geometry, the common-power fraction becomes the sole design variable. We prove that the communication-feasible set is either a closed interval or empty. Analytical outage expressions localize these endpoints, revealing a high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) floor-ceiling effect: common decoding dictates a common-power floor, while imperfect CSIT and SIC impose a private-decoding ceiling. For sensing, the conditional detection constraint is affine, preserving the interval structure. A geometry-matched common beam ensures monotonic detection improvement, reducing joint-feasibility check to the communication-feasible upper endpoint. Simulations validate our analysis, identifying regimes where common-stream-only sensing is viable.

papers.title: Characterizations and MacWilliams-Like Identities of Weakly Regular Bent Partitions
papers.abstract: Bent partitions play a significant role in the theory of bent functions. In this paper, we study weakly regular bent partitions, that is, all generated bent functions are weakly regular (called in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$). Let $\Gamma=\{A_{i}, i \in V_{m}\}$ be a bent partition of $V_{n}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$, where $V_{n}$ denotes an $n$-dimensional vector space over the prime field $\mathbb{F}_{p}$, $n$ is even, $m \leq \frac{n}{2}$, and $m \geq 2$ if $p=2$. We first characterize bent partition $\Gamma$ in terms of the duals of component functions of vectorial bent functions. In particular, we prove that if $p \neq 3$, then all bent functions generated by $\Gamma$ are regular. Building on the above result, we give characterizations of bent partition $\Gamma$ in terms of two classes of linear codes. When $n \geq 4$ and $m=\frac{n}{2}$, except for the case where $(p, n)=(2, 4)$ and $|A_{i_{0}}|=1$ for some $i_{0}$, we show that $\Gamma$ is obtained from a spread (after a shift). Particularly, any normal bent partition of $V_{n}$ of depth $p^{\frac{n}{2}}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$ must be obtained from a spread (after a shift), where $n \geq 4$. We establish the Macwilliams-like identities for bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$. Furthermore, if $p$ is odd, we present some nonexistence results on bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$.

papers.title: Channel dichotomies
papers.abstract: We study channel interconversion under non-signalling superchannels, where the asymptotic conversion rate is given by the ratio of the channel capacities. Our main result determines the second-order expansion of the optimal target length. Namely, when each channel has a single capacity-achieving dispersion, the coefficient is given by the inverse sesquinormal distribution, with parameters determined by the capacities and dispersions. The result extends state-dichotomy theory to channels: one superchannel approximates the target uniformly over inputs and maps every reference channel whose output is independent of its input to another such channel. As in state dichotomies, there are finite-error resonances where the second-order term vanishes, leaving an $O(\log n)$ remainder. Crucially, our new characterization cannot be obtained by concatenating channel coding and simulation protocols [Cao {\it et al.}~IEEE Trans.~Inf.~Theory (2024)]. Instead, the proof combines comparisons of binary hypothesis testing experiments with uniform Gaussian estimates and a construction that uses symmetry within type classes to satisfy the non-signalling constraints. Shared randomness assistance already suffices at first order, but we show that its second-order behaviour can differ strictly from the non-signalling case.

papers.title: Batch Universal Prediction via Conditional Additive Smoothing
papers.abstract: Modern language models motivate renewed interest in universal prediction problems in which a predictor can exploit previously observed data before predicting a fresh sequence. We study an idealized version of this setting by introducing \emph{batch regret}: a conditional analogue of classical average regret in which a predictor observes a batch of $n$ training sequences and is then evaluated on an independent test sequence generated by the same unknown source. Additive smoothing estimators, which add a bias to the observed token frequencies before predicting the next token, played a fundamental role as a simple prediction strategy with almost-optimal average regret for memoryless and Markov sources. Their equivalent under batch regret are the conditional additive smoothing estimators, which estimate the conditional distribution of the test sequence given the training batch. In this work, we study their asymptotical batch regret for binary memoryless and first-order Markov sources. For binary memoryless sources, we show how the optimal bias of the estimator, and consequently the corresponding batch regret, change as a function of the training batch size $n$, by extending the Poisson-based analysis of Krichevsky. For binary Markov sources with positive transitions, we characterize the leading coefficient of batch regret and its dependence on whether the initial law is known, free, or stationary. Finally, we introduce a R\'{e}nyi analogue of batch regret and identify the corresponding optimal predictors as conditional $\alpha$-NML estimators, thereby giving an operational interpretation to a conditional version of Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information.

papers.title: Rates and Nearly-Lossless State over a Multi-Access Channel with Causal State Information
papers.abstract: The problem of transmitting both data and state over a memoryless state-dependent multi-access channel with causal state information is addressed. The state comprises three independent components: a common component, which is revealed to both en- coders, and two private components, each of which is revealed to a different encoder. The data are to be recovered with arbitrarily-small probability of error, and the state sequence with arbitrarily-small symbol-error rate. Under the assumption that the capacity region in the absence of a state recon- struction constraint is nonempty, the capacity region is derived and is shown to be achievable using a Block-Markov coding scheme employing binning and superposition coding.

papers.title: Capacity Meets the Four Subspace Problem: Distributed Linear Computation and the Cross-Ratio
papers.abstract: $K$ users each observe a fixed linear function of common data over a finite field of characteristic $p$, and a server must recover another fixed linear function with zero error from one message sent by each user. The capacity, the minimum total number of symbols the users send per computed instance, depends only on the configuration of subspaces formed by these linear functions. We study the instance in which three users observe $\boldsymbol{a}$, $\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{a}+\boldsymbol{b}$ and the server wants $\boldsymbol{a}+\lambda\boldsymbol{b}$. The four functions span four lines in a plane with cross-ratio $\lambda$, the smallest instance of the four subspace problem of representation theory. It is the smallest configuration whose capacity is not determined by the dimensions of the subspaces formed by sums and intersections: these dimensions are the same for every $\lambda$, but the capacity depends on the cross-ratio and on the prime subfield. For the harmonic cross-ratios, $\lambda=-1$, $\lambda=2$ or $2\lambda=1$, it is $2$: every zero-error code reveals $(\boldsymbol{a},\boldsymbol{b})$ to the server, so no code beats having two users send their observations. For $\lambda$ outside the prime subfield it is the cut-set bound $3/2$, achieved by codes linear over the prime subfield, while codes linear over the field need $2$. For the other $\lambda$ in the prime subfield it lies in $[3p/(2p-1),2]$, so no code at any block length approaches the cut-set bound. The qualitative separation persists under vanishing error for uniform data: the cut-set bound is tight exactly for $\lambda$ outside the prime subfield. The four-line instance is also exact repair of one node of a $[4,2]$ MDS storage code, and the results translate to that setting.

papers.title: Instance-dependent sequential limits as an exact information ledger
papers.abstract: Instance-dependent limits for bandit regret, sequential tests, best-arm identification and Markov decision processes are proved by one chain. It runs from a divergence decomposition through data processing to a statistic, a testing step that turns a class guarantee into a requirement on the history, and optimization over alternatives and allocations. Only the first step is an identity. This work writes the chain as an exact ledger. By the chain rule, data processing loses exactly a conditional divergence, which vanishes for arms in natural exponential families at the per-arm counts and reward sums. A one-parameter family of martingale identities extends the decomposition to every tilt between two instances. The classical limits follow by relaxations with named defects. All defects but the asymptotic step's can be computed from an algorithm's own runs, the uniform quantification's only when the class guarantee is a number. On seven published sources, from movie ratings to engine replacement, the ledger locates the difference between standard algorithms and the classical limits. For identification among trained models and for Wald's test the largest term is usually the uniform quantification's.

papers.title: Robustness of Magic and the Directed Geometry of State Conversion
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce a state-space distance calibrated by stabilizer states based on the dual structure of the robustness of magic (RoM), and show that RoM is exactly represented as the distance to the free-state set. We then extend this geometry to state conversion by defining the directed conversion deficiency $C_{\mathcal F}$ as the distance between a target state and the set of states freely reachable from a given input state. The quantity $C_{\mathcal F}$ characterizes free convertibility and is related to the minimum stabilizer quasiprobability weight required to represent the conversion residual through the relation $1+2C_{\mathcal F}$. It also contains the conventional magic state resource lower bounds based on RoM and can detect stronger conversion obstructions. For single-qubit systems, we analytically construct a continuous family of mixed states with identical RoM but asymmetric convertibility.

papers.title: INLA for Adaptive UAV Sampling of Radio Environment Maps in IoT Networks: Prior Width Governs Accuracy and Calibration
papers.abstract: We study adaptive UAV sampling for radio environment map (REM) construction from non-Gaussian IoT observations. Integrated nested Laplace approximation(INLA) updates a Mat\'ern GMRF posterior, with waypoints selected by entropy pre-screening and Sherman--Morrison lookahead over the reachable set. We show that the likelihood-induced Skew-Normal correction has a sextic entropy effect, explaining its limited influence on waypoint selection. Across 19 retained ray-traced windows,Random and lawnmower sampling cost a median 18.0\% and 14.0\% more residual NMSE than posterior-informed sampling, equivalently reductions of 15.3\% and 12.3\% when referred to those baselines, while differences among informative rules remain unresolved. Widening the prior shadowing standard deviation from 6.0 to 10.025\,dB improves NMSE and credible-interval coverage, with monotone improvement over a 4--16\,dB sweep on this corpus and no observed turning point, although overconfidence persists. Online width estimation from the UAV's own counts yields about 6.5\,dB without recovering the gain. Across 30 measured LoRaWAN propagation windows paired with simulated counts and scored only on received cells, the margin over non-adaptive sampling reproduces, the training-derived width minimizes the tested interval score, and GP-UCB has nominally $3$--$5\%$ lower NMSE. The results show substantial, corpus-dependent sensitivity to prior specification, while fine differences among acquisition rules have limited or unresolved effects, the preferred width depends on the corpus, scored cells and model mismatch.

papers.title: Estimation of Quantum Umlaut Information
papers.abstract: Quantifying correlations is important for understanding how quantum states and channels support information processing. Quantum umlaut information $U$ connects such correlations to reliability in hypothesis testing and certain communication settings, but its known formulas require classical descriptions of the underlying states. To estimate correlations without these descriptions, we introduce measured quantum umlaut information $U^M$ by replacing Umegaki relative entropy with measured relative entropy. Its variational formulation leads to a quantum generative adversarial framework for estimating $U^M$ from measurement statistics of unknown bipartite states and classical-quantum channels. This framework optimizes reference states and measurements without reconstructing the target states or channel outputs. For classical-quantum channels, it also optimizes the input probabilities. We further analyze the relation between $U^M$ and $U$, deriving a state-dependent gap bound and characterizing equality for full-rank bipartite states. Numerical simulations show trained estimates close on average to independently computed numerical references for $U^M$ across the tested states and channels. These estimates could help assess how well quantum memories preserve correlations and how noise or drift affects input-output dependence in quantum transmitters and state-preparation devices.

papers.title: Sparse descent subspace-Newton thresholding algorithm for sparse optimization problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a sparse descent direction derived from the Newton direction within a low-dimensional subspace for sparse optimization problems. Building upon this direction and incorporating hard thresholding and orthogonal projection, we develop a novel algorithm termed the sparse descent subspace-Newton thresholding (SDSNT) algorithm. We further establish its global convergence under the restricted isometry property $\delta_{3k}\leq \sqrt{3/20}$ of the measurement matrix. Numerical experiments on random sparse vector recovery and audio signal reconstruction reveal that SDSNT achieves comparable performance to several state-of-the-art algorithms. Notably, relative to most of them, it delivers superior recovery at high sparsity levels and improved efficiency at low sparsity levels.

papers.title: On $t$-designs supported by self-orthogonal codes
papers.abstract: We study self-orthogonal $t$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ designs satisfying the condition that the codes generated by the designs are self-orthogonal codes whose codewords of minimum weight $k$ correspond to the blocks. A classification of such designs is given under the conditions that $t\geq \lfloor k/4\rfloor+1\geq2$ and $t \le 11$. This yields a classification of self-orthogonal codes of minimum weight $k$ whose codewords of minimum weight form a $t$-design under the same conditions.

papers.title: On approximate support versions of Donoho--Stark uncertainty principles for $k$-Hadamard operators
papers.abstract: In this paper we present results related to Donoho--Stark type uncertainty principles that were proved in the article "The uncertainty principle: variations on a theme" by Wigderson and Wigderson for $k$-Hadamard operators in the finite-dimensional setting. Namely, the authors showed that Donoho-Stark principles can be generalized to versions for approximate supports with respect to norms $\ell^{p}$ for $p=1$ and $p=2$. In the second case they assumed the so-called speciality condition, namely that a suitable matrix satisfies $A^{*}A = kI$. First we show that such theorems cannot be generalized to $p>1$ if matrices are not special $k$-Hadamard. Next we prove Donoho-Stark type principle for special $k$-Hadamard operators for $\ell^{p}$ norms within the range $1\leq p\leq 2$. Finally, we show that such theorems are false for $p>2$ even in the presence of the speciality condition.

papers.title: Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) embodies a foundational paradigm for sequential decision-making in the face of uncertainty. The rapid growth of model complexity in emerging applications has significantly amplified the challenges of achieving data-efficient RL, particularly in sample-starved scenarios where data collection may be costly, time-consuming, or even high-stakes. Consequently, understanding and improving the data efficiency of RL algorithms has become a central problem of both fundamental theoretical interest and practical importance. Despite decades of research, the statistical underpinnings of RL remained remarkably underdeveloped until relatively recently, particularly in the finite-sample regimes most relevant to modern practice. Over the past few years, there has been a surge of activity advancing the frontiers of non-asymptotic statistical RL theory, drawing on ideas from high-dimensional statistics and probability, information theory, and statistical learning theory. In this monograph, we present a non-asymptotic treatment for RL based on tabular Markov decision processes, focusing on three canonical sampling mechanisms --- RL with a generative model, online RL, and offline RL --- together with two algorithmic paradigms: model-based and model-free approaches. Centered around non-asymptotic sample complexity analysis, our treatment emphasizes minimax-optimal algorithm design, particularly methods that attain statistical optimality without significant burn-in costs, as well as sharp statistical characterizations of several widely used RL algorithms. Whenever possible, we provide largely self-contained analyses together with intuitive explanations. We also briefly discuss several extensions, such as robust RL, competitive multi-agent RL, federated RL, uncertainty quantification, and RL from human feedback.

papers.title: Extremal character spectra of finite projective systems
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal M$ be a finite spanning multiset of points in ${\rm PG}(k-1,q)$, and let ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ be its character function. For $1\le r\le k$, we study the maximum number of distinct values attained by ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ on the codimension-$r$ flats under a total-multiplicity budget. The spectrum is subject to two natural upper bounds, whose extremal cases lead respectively to $r$-maximum character spectrum ($r$-MCS) and $r$-full character spectrum ($r$-FCS) systems. We establish the existence of $r$-FCS systems in a broad parameter range, and solve the size-constrained extremal problem completely when $r=k-1$, including the minimum-cost multiplicity profiles. For $1\le r<k$, put $M_r=\qbinom{k}{r}$ and $B_r=\qbinom{k-1}{r}$. The minimum size $\nu_r(k,q)$ of an $r$-MCS system satisfies \[\left\lceil\frac{\binom{M_r}{2}}{B_r}\right\rceil\le \nu_r(k,q)\le \binom{M_r-1}{2}+\frac{q^k-q^{k-r}}{q-1}.\] The upper bound is at most $\binom{M_r}{2}$, strictly less when $r\le k-2$, and exact when $r=k-1$. Its proof applies positive additive labelings to the complement of one flat, whose trace is empty while all remaining traces are distinct. For $r=1$, we improve the known upper bounds on the minimum length of such systems. We also develop global moment identities and local flat-incidence bounds that impose strong structural constraints on large character spectra. Under the projective-system correspondence, complementary character spectra are the support-weight spectra of $r$-dimensional subcodes.

papers.title: Embodied Movable Antennas
papers.abstract: This paper introduces embodied movable antennas (MAs), a new MA architecture that rethinks the source of antenna mobility. Unlike conventional MAs that rely on dedicated antenna actuators, embodied MAs harness the mechanical degrees of freedom already present in physical agents to reconfigure antenna position and orientation. We distinguish two modes of embodied MAs: task-coupled and task-preserving. Focusing on the latter, we show how wireless channels can be reconfigured by exploiting task-equivalent host configurations without altering the prescribed physical task. Using a redundant robotic manipulator as a canonical realization, we characterize the intrinsically coupled antenna translation and orientation induced by task-preserving self-motion and derive an exact Fourier representation of the resulting multipath channel. Our analysis reveals that the wireless value of embodied mobility depends not merely on how far an antenna can move, but on which configurations remain feasible under the physical task and how their coupled motion interacts with polarization and multipath propagation. Building on this insight, we develop a cross-task antenna mounting design that enables wireless adaptation with a fixed physical installation. Numerical results demonstrate substantial communication gains through task-preserving motion. These findings establish mechanical redundancy as a new, quantifiable resource for wireless channel reconfiguration.

papers.title: Sample complexity of quantum resource testing via one-shot quantum blurring
papers.abstract: Quantum resource testing is a fundamental primitive of quantum information processing, profoundly connected to resource manipulation. Its goal is to discriminate $n$ copies of a given resourceful state $\rho$ from all free (i.e., resourceless) states; key instances for applications are entanglement testing and quantum magic testing. The asymptotic characterisation relies on the recently proven Generalised Quantum Stein's Lemma (GQSL), which establishes the rate of decay of the false negative error probability for a fixed false positive error probability. This result, however, is intrinsically asymptotic and thus can provide no finite-resource guarantees, which makes its practical implications unclear. Here, we establish the first rigorous finite-$n$ bounds on quantum resource testing and hence quantum resource manipulation, thus strengthening the GQSL and providing explicit estimates on the number of copies needed to achieve a prescribed performance. As notable consequences, we obtain (a) the convergence of the regularised R\'enyi relative entropies of a resource, which settles the important open problem from [Fang/Hayashi, arXiv:2508.12901, IEEE ToIT 72:6, 2026]; and (b) the first sample-complexity bound for asymmetric resource testing: for any fixed false positive error probability, a false negative error probability of at most $\delta$ can be achieved with $n=O\left(\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{D^\infty(\rho\|\mathcal F)}\right)$ copies of $\rho$, in the limit where $\delta \to 0$.
